subject: PIPELINE chokepoint: high p95/p99 on checkout - coordination & customer note
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@fixify.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: ops@fixify.com
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden latency & partial failures on checkout pipeline

Jonas / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in latency on the checkout pipeline at ~08:50 PT — p95 jumped from 180ms to ~3.8s and p99 is trending >9s. A subset (~2.1%) of tokenized requests are returning 5xxs from your Gen API. This is impacting session timeouts and a noticeable uptick in abandoned checkouts for our customers.

We attached a small sample of request traces and a short metrics dump (fixify-request-logs-20280809.zip). Our SRE says it looks like a service-side slowdown rather than client spikes on our side. Can you confirm receipt and give an ETA for the first update? We can join a bridge immediately.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Site Reliability
Fixify

--
Attachment: fixify-request-logs-20280809.zip (traces + metric snippet)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: FWD: sudden latency & partial failures on checkout pipeline

David / Karthik — forwarding Fixify's alert. Immediate asks:
- Quick triage to identify whether this is a serving runtime regression, cache evaporation, or downstream queueing.
- If it's capacity-related, can we do a temporary routing rule to shift Fixify to the graceful-fallback model (lower-cost but more stable variant) while we stabilize?
- Need a short customer-facing note (1 paragraph) and an ETA for next status update (we should aim for 2pm PT if possible).

Marissa — looping you in for customer comms/expectations.

I'll open a bridge if David confirms.

Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: sudden latency & partial failures on checkout pipeline

Quick summary after 35m triage:
- Observed behavior: sudden p95/p99 increase across several clusters serving Fixify. Error spike corresponds to requests that hit a multi-fanout path and then wait for slow adaptors (~200-400ms added tail), amplifying to seconds when combined with KV cache misses.
- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: aggressive KV cache eviction during a rolling rebalancing + an unexpected increase in token fanout for a specific model variant. Not seeing obvious new deploys in the last 24h.
- Short-term mitigations (can do now):
  1) Flip Fixify routing to the model-variant with local-prefix-cache enabled (will lower throughput slightly but stabilizes p95).
  2) Apply a temporary throttle on multi-fanout queries (config change).
  3) If needed, escalate to capacity-burst for that customer for 60m (requires approval).

I've attached profiler output and the KV eviction snapshot. I can run a bridge at 10:30 if you want.

Attachments: profiling-20280809.log, kv-eviction-snapshot.csv

-david
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: sudden latency & partial failures on checkout pipeline

Thanks David — good triage. Product questions / constraints we need to surface before we change routing:
1) What is the measurable drop in throughput for the local-prefix-cache variant? Need ballpark numbers so we can explain tradeoffs to Fixify (e.g., 8-12% throughput reduction vs p95 improvement).
2) Is the multi-fanout throttle safe for Fixify's common request patterns? We need to avoid functional regressions for their checkout UX.
3) For the longer-term fix, is persisting the prefetch cache across rolling rebalances feasible in the 2-4 week roadmap, or does it require a larger runtime change? If the latter, we should commit to a pragmatic short-term config we can operate in prod for a month.

Action asks: David — can you provide the throughput delta for the local-prefix-cache flip and whether the throttle can be scoped to only the problematic multi-fanout path? If yes, we'll prepare the customer note explaining the short-term tradeoff and the longer-term roadmap ask.

Karthik
Head of Product, Serving Runtime

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fixify.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: sudden latency & partial failures on checkout pipeline

Elena — thanks for flagging and for the traces. Short note from us: we have an SRE lead investigating and are preparing a short mitigation that we can apply within ~20-30 minutes. We will:

- Apply a routing fallback for your traffic to a model variant with local-prefix-cache enabled (this reduces the risk of cache-evaporation-related tails). We estimate an initial stabilization within ~10 minutes of the change.
- Scope a temporary throttle on the multi-fanout path to prevent amplification while we investigate the root cause.

We plan a status update at 2:00 PM PT with either stable metrics or next steps. Would you like a bridge at 12:30 PT?

Below is the draft customer message (please review / approve):

--- DRAFT CUSTOMER NOTE ---
Hi Elena — we’re actively investigating the latency spike you reported. Our SREs have identified amplification caused by cache misses and multi-fanout routing for a specific model variant.

Actions we are taking now: routing your production traffic to a variant with local-prefix-cache enabled and applying a temporary throttle to the multi-fanout path. We expect these changes to materially stabilize tail latency within ~10–30 minutes. We will follow up with a status update at 2:00 PM PT.

If helpful, we can open a joint bridge now (we have SRE bandwidth to do 12:30 PT).

--- end draft ---

Marissa / David / Karthik — please hit reply with any edits. I’ll send as soon as I get a thumbs up.

Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
